 Ghana's Chance to Bounce Back in AFCON 2027 Qualifying After Poor Start
 After missing AFCON 2025, Ghana faces a crucial doubleheader against Somalia with a new head coach and several key players returning to the squad.
 The Black Stars Aim to Bounce Back After Carlos Queiroz's Departure as Key Players Return to Inspire Hope.
 Ghana has a golden opportunity to get its AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign back on track. The Black Stars will face Somalia , one of the most vulnerable teams in Group C, knowing they must collect points to keep their hopes of returning to Africa's premier international tournament alive after missing the 2025 edition .
 Don't Miss the Road to AFCON 2027 Qualifiers on beIN SPORTS! 
 TWO MATCHES TO TURN THEIR CAMPAIGN AROUND
 Ghana heads into this doubleheader under pressure after losing its first two qualifying matches : a 2-0 defeat against Ivory Coast and a 4-2 loss to Gambia. As a result, the Black Stars remain pointless and must take advantage of their two games against Somalia to get back into the qualification race.
 The first match will take place on November 12, with the return fixture scheduled for November 16. Both games will be played on Ghanaian soil. Somalia has also lost its first two matches and sits at the bottom of the standings alongside Ghana, although its goal difference is slightly better.
 Watch Ghana vs. Somalia in the AFCON 2027 Qualifiers this Thursday, November 12, on beIN SPORTS! 
 Watch Somalia vs. Ghana in the AFCON 2027 Qualifiers this Monday, November 16, on beIN SPORTS! 
 KEY PLAYERS RETURN AS NEW COACH TAKES CHARGE
 Carlos Queiroz's departure , agreed upon on October 1 following the defeats against Ivory Coast and Gambia, paved the way for Kim Lars Björkegren , who has taken over as interim head coach with the task of rescuing Ghana's qualifying campaign.
 His first squad features several important returns: Jordan Ayew , back after recovering from a groin injury; Mohammed Kudus , who had not played for Ghana in 2026 due to fitness issues; Daniel Kofi Kyereh , returning to the national team for the first time since December 2022; Alidu Seidu and Mohammed Salisu . Brighton forward Ibrahim Osman is also among the notable names.
 CAN GHANA STILL QUALIFY FOR AFCON 2027?
 The situation is challenging, but qualification remains possible. The top two teams in Group C will advance to the final tournament , which will feature 24 nations and take place in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
 Ivory Coast and Gambia lead the group with six points each , while Ghana and Somalia remain without a point. Securing all six points against Somalia would therefore be crucial to keeping the Black Stars' qualification hopes alive.
 After missing AFCON 2025 in Morocco, the four-time African champions have another opportunity to reclaim their place among the continent's top national teams. The doubleheader against Somalia could mark the beginning of the comeback Ghana desperately needs.
 GHANA'S AFCON 2027 FUTURE IS ON THE LINE
 CRUCIAL SHOWDOWN AGAINST SOMALIA: Ghana must take advantage of the November 12 and 16 doubleheader to claim its first six points and stay in the qualification race.
 KEY PLAYERS RETURN TO THE SQUAD: Jordan Ayew, Mohammed Kudus, Daniel Kofi Kyereh, Alidu Seidu and Mohammed Salisu are all back in the squad.
 NEW ERA AFTER CARLOS QUEIROZ: Kim Lars Björkegren takes over as interim head coach, tasked with turning around Ghana's poor start and leading the Black Stars back to AFCON after missing the 2025 tournament.
